reviews.t: Helps me to have a "Rachel" LOL
reviews.x: I finally found a product to give me that slight "bend" that I needed to make me look like Jennifer Aniston (I wish!). I recently cut my, somewhat long, baby fine and thinning hair into that style known as "The Rachel". The one that Jennifer Aniston made so popular. It is long all over, but graduated lengths in the front. This style needs a large round brush to acheive that slight bend at the ends.  I am terrible with a round brush and blow dryer. I tried a blow dryer with a round brush attachme

i LOVE this thing!  after six years of daily use, it is still going strong!  sometimes the bristles don't always hold short fine hair very well, but a very light spritz of hair spray before you start will take care of that problem.  one cool feature is the square slot in the blue "cool tip" end (you have to look for it cuz it blends in with the other curved indentations all around the edge) - if you turn the tip so that slot lines up with a row of bristles, you can slide the bristles out
Works great everytime. Warms up quickly and gets hot enough.  Just wish it had an auto shutoff. Don't purchase from a beauty supply..they want 2.5 times the price you will pay online.

Although this curling brush is said to have a one inch barrel, it somehow seemed much larger than the 3/4 inch barrel that I already owned. It heats up quickly & does a nice job, but the tip that you hold on the end could be a bit larger. It also gets hot & can burn you if not extremely careful. Even still, I'm glad that I purchased it.

This little curler is perfect for SHORT hair--like pixie short hair. If you have longer hair, this is going to get all tangled up in it. The smaller barrel is just right to give my pixie haircut the perkiness that it needed. I love it.

I agree that it is hard to find this kind of heating iron with the brush teeth, so I ordered this thinking it would be more up to date than the v. old slow-to-heat conair I have.  well, this Helen of Troy heating iron is not any better than the old ones I have.  it is sloooow to heat up !!!  it also feels cheaper than my old versions.  and although it has a plastic cap on the end of the heated part, it seems a little on the skimpy side and I would feel safer and less nervous if the protective ca
I have a hard time finding heated curling brushes these days, and this one works well.  I do wish it had automatic shut-off, but other than that it is fine.

reviews.t: My hair is chin-length and fine, not thick
reviews.x: I have been using these for years, but the last order - 2 of them, purchased less than 6 months ago - was so disappointing. The first one just fell apart, a screw or something that holds the blue plastic end in place came loose so the end wouldn't tighten, bristles [combs?] would fall out. I gave up and threw it away. The second one, which I have been using for about 3 weeks, has been limping along for a couple of weeks. There's a short or something to the heating element. The light will be on,
This is the best curling iron I ever had in my life and I've had a lot of them. All different sizes and types. I do have fine hair but a lot of it and this is the perfect curling iron for that.

reviews.t: Using this brush iron for years!
reviews.x: I discovered this brush iron at least 15 years ago and have been using it (and replacements) for all these years to finish off my hair after I dry it with a dryer.  It is NOT a dryer...rather a hair curling or straightening out iron for your hair depending on what type of hair you have and style you want.  It is easy to use and does not burn your scalp like some of the other types of irons available.  I can't be without it and use it daily.  The smaller the barrel, the tighter the curls...so dec

reviews.t: Not the same as in the past
reviews.x: Have ordered this same Brush Iron multiple times over many years.  Past versions worked perfectly for several years, but the latest versions have very fragile "brush" inserts and this current one is slow to heat, heating to a medium-low temperature. (I have taken the new brush inserts and replaced the broken ones on the old curler.)  Will not purchase this item again.

reviews.t: Bristles start breaking off within a month of usage.
reviews.x: Edited 5/13/2016:  I've used this product for years and it worked great with longer bristles.  It always had a tendency for the bristles to get brittle due to the heat of the curling iron,, and then the bristles break off very easily.  The last two I purchased, the bristles starting breaking off within a month of usage.  It used to take several months of use for this to happen.  The plastic you are using on the bristles is defective.  Please remedy this.  They recently shortened the bristles and
It may not be the best one ever made, but you can't find these anywhere anymore.  I am satisfied with the product and was also pleasantly suprised at how lightweight it is.

reviews.t: Rows of plastic teeth are extremely brittle and break easily
reviews.x: I'm finally writing my review 6/2016. My hair is shoulder length and very thick. I have three 1 1/2 inch barrel Helen of Troy model 1514's purchased between 2011 and 2014. All 3 still heat up very hot, each iron has 10 rows of teeth around the barrel; between all three irons there are 30 rows of teeth, 20 rows are completely devoid of any teeth, only  2 rows remain whole. Beware, the teeth on all three were immediately brittle and within 3 weeks of each purchase I only had about half of the teet

I have a graduated bob and bleached (level 12) hair. This means varied lengths, from about 4" to 10", and damaged hair that must be treated very tenderly. Because I favor a smooth underswept style, I was using my flatiron to achieve that look, but first I had to blowdry my hair or my natural wave would still turn through the ironing. A double process is a pain, and the blowdrying takes away the sheen from my hair, making it look lifeless.  The brush iron is easy to hold and does not dimi

I love this curling brush.  It gives so much body and fullness to my straight hair.  Some curling brushes are too small and makes my hair unruly with tight, little curls.  The 1 inch diameter gives soft curls.  I also purchased the 1 1/2 inch diameter and love it even more!  I have to buy it online as I can't find it at any stores in my area.

I love this curling brush.  It gives so much body and fullness to my straight hair.  Some curling brushes are too small and makes my hair unruly with tight, little curls.  The 1 inch diameter gives soft curls.  I also purchased the 1 1/2 inch diameter and love it even more!  I have to buy it online as I can't find it at any stores in my area.

This curling brush is great for fine and/or thin hair.  It gets hot enough to do the job, but not so hot that it would burn your hair. The tip only gets warm, not so hot that you'd burn your fingers while guiding it. My only suggestion for any improvement would be to make the cord a bit longer. It also is very easy to clean; if you turn the tip, you can slide out the individual brush strips (one at a time) to enable you to wash those.  I would not recommend doing anything other than wiping down

reviews.t: Not up to previous quality standards.
reviews.x: I've used this brand for years, to smooth my frizzy hair, and add a bit of curl. This one is not a great as the ones I've had in the past; the tip, which spins freely has no apparent means to tighten it. As there is a groove in the tip that allows one to remove the brush pieces one at a time for cleaning, and I can't tighten it, I am always finding the brush pieces on the floor or in my bag. The tip and handle aren't exactly flush with the iron, so one or two strands of hair get caught, and pull

reviews.t: Helen of Troy 1514 Brush Iron stopped working after less than 90 days!
reviews.x: We purchased (2) of the Helen of Troy 1514 Brush Irons on November 29, 2017. One of them stopped working on February 19, 2018 and would not heat up on Low or Hi.  We've had previous models that lasted for years, still heated up and were used till all the bristles broke off. We will see how the second one performs as I am cautiously optomistic Amazons return time frame ended on January 29, 2018 and so we are still looking for information on the manufacturers warranty. Hopefully it will be honored

I have short, fine, permed, blond hair.  The "brush" on this iron holds my hair in place on the rod without tangling it.  It gets pretty hot to allow quick styling so you must be careful not to touch the iron itself.  The protective tip should be a little bit longer to allow a better grasp with no chance of burning your fingers.  Other than that, I think this is a great curling iron.  It's hard to find an iron that works well for fine hair.  This one does the job quite well.

This is exactly what I needed. The size is perfect for my growing-out hair, and makes it so much more manageable. It gets really hot on high, and a little less on low. I have a 1" brush iron, but it's difficult to work with, and this 1/2" is perfect. I remember Helen of Troy products from quite a while back, and they're as good now as they were then!
Great item-heats up fast and has 2 settings.  Perfect for fast touch ups!

reviews.t: Does not get hot enough to curl my hair!
reviews.x: This curling iron is very small in length and also in width of the handle part.  I recently had a very short haircut and thought the 1/2 inch might be good, but this just does not get hot enough to curl.  It has only an off/low/high switch.  Perhaps if you had very thin, fine hair it might be hot enough for some, but I have never had a curling iron/brush that did not get really hot!  I am continuing to use my old 3/4 inch Conair curling brush.  I threw this box away, so will donate this to local

I just washed and curled my 81 year old Mom’s hair with the Helen of Troy 1512 Brush Iron 1/2 inch. It worked great. My Mom can no longer go to a hair dresser so I (female 55 year old daughter) cut and styles her hair. I could not find a half inch brush iron in stores so this worked perfectly. Granted, I used this for the first time today, but I have have high hopes for the future.

claims.text: Many reviewers praise the product's performance, saying it works well and heats up quickly.
Several reviewers note the bristles or plastic teeth are brittle and break off easily over time.
Some reviewers wish the product had an automatic shut-off feature.
Reviewers describe the product as well-suited for short or fine hair, with the smaller barrel being ideal for pixie cuts.
A few reviewers report slow heating or that the unit only reaches a medium-low temperature.

qa.q: Does it get hot enough to actually straighten thick hair?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: How durable is the barrel and bristles over time?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on durability: some report bristles breaking off within a month [1] and fragile brush inserts on newer versions [6], while another reports it still going strong after six years of daily use [2]. One review also describes a unit falling apart with bristles falling out [5].

claims.text: Bristles start breaking off within a month of usage.
The latest versions have very fragile brush inserts.
After six years of daily use, it is still going strong.
One unit fell apart with bristles falling out.

qa.q: Is it comfortable to hold and use for longer styling sessions?
qa.answer: Reviews are mixed on comfort for longer sessions: some say the tip only gets warm and won't burn your fingers [2], while others say the protective tip should be longer or larger and can get hot and burn you if not careful [3][6].
